<description>
`invalidateblock` returns `null` even when the block was not invalidated because the RPC does not pay attention to `Chainstate::InvalidateBlock()` return value. If there is a problem disconnecting the block (for example, the undo data is corrupt), the chain remains partially rolled back when telling the user that the operation succeeded. This creates an error in every failure case, including the genesis block case, and makes RPC look at the return value. The error reports a failed block and how far the chain was rolled back before the block returned.

Fixes #36546
</description>

[2026-10-20] c:6294852607 comment by yusufyildiz34:
Reviewed the diff; I have not built or tested the branch.

Concept makes sense — `invalidateblock` reporting success after a partial
rollback is clearly wrong, and routing the failures through `state` so the
existing RPC error path picks them up is cleaner than patching the RPC helper.

Two things on the implementation.

**The error message in the third hunk names the wrong block.**

```cpp
if (m_chain.Contains(*to_mark_failed)) {
    return state.Error(strprintf("Block %s was not invalidated because it is still in the active chain (interrupted?)", pindex->GetBlockHash().ToString()));
}
```

The condition tests `to_mark_failed`, but the message prints `pindex`.
`to_mark_failed` is reassigned inside the disconnect loop
(`to_mark_failed = disconnected_tip;`), so once at least one iteration has run
the two are different blocks — `to_mark_failed` is the last disconnected block,
a descendant of `pindex`. In that case the message names a block that may well
have been disconnected successfully, while the block actually still in the
chain goes unnamed. `to_mark_failed->GetBlockHash()` would match the condition.

**`state.Error()` for the genesis case.**

`ModeState` in `consensus/validation.h` documents `M_ERROR` as
`//!< run-time error`, and the RPC maps `IsError()` to `RPC_DATABASE_ERROR`.
So passing the genesis hash now returns
`-20 Database error: Cannot invalidate genesis block`. That is a caller error,
not a runtime one, and the neighbouring "Block not found" case in the same
helper uses `RPC_INVALID_ADDRESS_OR_KEY` (-5). Rejecting height 0 in the RPC
helper next to the existing `LookupBlockIndex()` check, with
`RPC_INVALID_PARAMETER`, would give a more accurate code and keep `M_ERROR`
meaning an actual internal failure — which the disconnect-failure hunk
legitimately is.

nit: the two commits have near-identical subjects, and the second largely
reverts the first's changes to `src/rpc/blockchain.cpp` and the functional
test. They look like a fixup pair that wants squashing; both commit bodies are
also empty.

Does this want a release note? `invalidateblock` now throws where it previously
returned null.

Finally, @l0rinc's point about documenting the partial-state behaviour instead
of adding regression code is still open — if that direction wins, most of the
above is moot.
